neighbours.label: the word-class terms verb, noun, adjective and adverb (and 形容词), as opposed to other words about language in the same frames (word, phrase, term, full stop) and other grammar terms (plural, derivative)
fire: Yesterday takes a verb in the past tense in this exercise.
The word 'run' can be a noun as well as a title.
Swedish adjective endings agree with what follows them.
Put the adjective before the thing it describes.
Definitions of glimmer: - noun - a faint light.
English 'swiftly' is an adverb formed from 'swift'.
Etymology: from Latin, as a noun in the fourteenth century.
这个句子里的形容词用得很好。
quiet: Yesterday takes a full stop at the end in this exercise.
The word 'run' can be a name as well as a title.
Swedish plurals agree with what follows them.
Put the phrase before the thing it describes.
Definitions of glimmer: - see also - a faint light.
English 'swiftly' is a derivative formed from 'swift'.
Etymology: from Latin, as a phrase in the fourteenth century.
这个句子里的词语用得很好。

notes: Card: ' verb' x5, 'verb' x5, ' adjective' x4, ' noun' x4, 'noun' x2, plus ' novel' x2 and 詞. Probes: 0.32-0.86 on the English terms, 0.24 on 形容词; ' word', ' definition', ' sentence' 0.06 or less, ' poem' 0.13, ' novel' 0.16. Output promotes ' form', '-form', ' version', which suggests 'form of a word'; not tested.
